splVariants.notes: Draft. Splunk's Integrated Enterprise Value for Cisco data page lists cisco:cybervision:devices under the Cisco Catalyst Add-on for Splunk. https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-cloud-platform/get-started/get-data-in/10.5.2605/cisco-source-type-benefit/integrated-enterprise-value-for-cisco-data Splunkbase 7538 is that add-on: app id TA_cisco_catalyst, title Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk, archive_status live (checked 2026-11-05). The older Cisco Cyber Vision Add-on (Splunkbase 5748, TA-cisco_cybervision) is also still live; the Cisco app navigator lists 5748 as a legacy uid and 7538 as the add-on for this sourcetype. Field names id, deviceType and group.label are from the Cisco Cyber Vision Center API device record (Get Device Details, API 3.0.0-5.5.0). https://developer.cisco.com/docs/cyber-vision/get-device-details/ No sample event ships with the add-on, so check that the input writes the device record unchanged. Cyber Vision groups play the role of Nozomi zones; the device record has no top-level vendor field (vendor sits in normalizedProperties), so this variant counts device types instead of vendors.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `nozomi` (UC-14.9.1)** — Planned work for 'OT Asset Discovery and Inventory Tracking' shifts `total_devices`, `vendors` over `span=1h` while `zone` remains in-scope.  Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `dc` on `nozomi:nn_asset`** — Scheduled automation elevates `device_summary` without crossing configured threshold for UC-14.9.1. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `zone`** — Health checks in `nozomi` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `nozomi:nn_asset`** — First 48h baseline for UC-14.9.1 on `zone` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `zone`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: `Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk` (`TA_cisco_catalyst`, Splunkbase 7538) · `Nozomi Networks Universal Add-on` (Splunkbase 6905).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=cisco:cybervision:devices` · Nozomi: `sourcetype=nozomi:nn_asset`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
**Cyber Vision:** Configure Splunk Add-On with API token from Cyber Vision Center; add "Devices" input with polling interval (e.g. 3600s). **Nozomi:** Configure Universal Add-on with Guardian/Vantage API credentials; enable the `nn_asset` data input. Both platforms passively discover assets — use device data as the authoritative OT asset inventory for compliance and security programs.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=nozomi sourcetype="nozomi:nn_asset"
| stats dc(id) as total_devices, dc(vendor) as vendors, values(vendor) as vendor_list by zone
| eval device_summary=total_devices." devices from ".vendors." vendors"
| table zone, total_devices, vendors, vendor_list, device_summary
```

Understanding this SPL

**OT Asset Discovery and Inventory Tracking** — You cannot secure what you do not know exists. OT network security platforms (Cisco Cyber Vision, Nozomi Guardian) passively discover every device on your OT network via deep packet inspection of industrial protocols — PLCs, HMIs, drives, field devices — and builds an always-current inventory with vendor, model, firmware, serial number, and rack slot. This eliminates manual spreadsheets and provides the foundation for all other OT security use cases.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=cisco:cybervision:devices` · Nozomi: `sourcetype=nozomi:nn_asset`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): `Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk` (`TA_cisco_catalyst`, Splunkbase 7538) · `Nozomi Networks Universal Add-on` (Splunkbase 6905). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: nozomi; **sourcetype**: nozomi:nn_asset. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=nozomi, sourcetype="nozomi:nn_asset". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by zone** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **device_summary** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Pipeline stage (see **OT Asset Discovery and Inventory Tracking**): table zone, total_devices, vendors, vendor_list, device_summary

Step 3 — Validate
Run the search for a time range that should include both routine and change activity, then compare the same assets, flows, and alerts in the Cisco Cyber Vision UI and in Nozomi Guardian or CMC, matching whichever source the event came from. Reconcile severities, counts, and key fields in both tools.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Asset count single value; vendor breakdown pie chart; device table with firmware versions; site comparison bar chart.
grandmaExplanation: We use our network security tool’s inventory in Splunk so we know which OT devices exist and how they change over time, which is the basis for protecting them.
